articles.headline: Fantasy football: Ranking the best, worst landing spots for Jonathan Taylor
articles.description: It may be just a matter of time before Taylor is dealt, so Michael F. Florio ranks his potential destinations.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール：ジョナサン・テイラーの移籍先ベスト＆ワースト予想
articles.descriptionJa: テイラーのトレードは時間の問題かもしれない。マイケル・F・フロリオが、彼の潜在的な移籍先をランク付けする。
articles.body:
There are two factors that go into determining the best and worst fantasy football landing spots for Jonathan Taylor.

The first is what is best for Taylor. I fully believe he is an elite talent and will succeed anywhere. And any team trading for him has to be in a better situation than the Indianapolis Colts, who have traded their top offensive lineman. They have also had poor quarterback play and often trail, which means a negative game script for the running game. However, Taylor is also going to crater the fantasy value of the running backs on whichever team he is dealt to. That should be considered as well.

Best Jonathan Taylor landing spots

1. Minnesota Vikings: I would expect any team that acquires Taylor to use him plenty, but the Vikings and their style of play make a lot of sense. They have run the ball at the sixth-highest rate this season. They want to establish the run and trust their defense. Minnesota has created the third-most yards before contact on RB carries, so its offensive line is creating running lanes for the backs.

This is a situation where Taylor would get to come in and become the immediate focal point on a team very much in the hunt. It could also help open things up in the passing game, which Justin Jefferson managers would enjoy. Lastly, neither of the Vikings' current running backs is a great fantasy option. Since Jordan Mason returned, neither he nor Aaron Jones Sr. has scored seven fantasy points in a game.

2. Seattle Seahawks: This would ruin the fantasy values of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet, but neither has provided much anyway. The Seahawks have struggled to create consistent running lanes, as evidenced by their 0.6 yards before contact per carry (NFL average: 0.9); however, we should see improvements there with recent acquisition Quenton Nelson on the offensive line. This is the rare instance where Taylor would not be the focal point of opposing defenses, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the perimeter.

3. Cincinnati Bengals: This would hurt in fantasy as it would take Chase Brown out as a weekly option. However, the Bengals' offense would be the NFL version of the "Monstars" with Taylor added. Good luck stacking the box and leaving Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase to run wild in the secondary.

4. Washington Commanders: The Commanders are creating running lanes, but their backs have struggled to consistently produce. Taylor would immediately change that, on a team that has a ton of touches up for grabs. Taylor getting to run the option with Jayden Daniels should make fantasy managers of either player salivate. We have yet to see Daniels paired with a dominant running back.

5. New England Patriots: The Patriots' backs might produce at times for fantasy, but they have struggled all season. Both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson have averaged under 4 yards per carry. In fact, both have negative rush EPAs on the season. articles.headline: Giants try to end 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia, as Eagles turn to 3rd-string QB Milton
articles.description: — The New York Giants could practically mark an ‘L’ on their schedule each season as soon as they saw their date in Philadelphia.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツ、フィラデルフィアで13連敗阻止へ、イーグルズは第3控えQBミルトンを起用
articles.descriptionJa: — ニューヨーク・ジャイアンツにとって、フィラデルフィアでの試合日程を見るだけで、毎シーズンの予定表に「敗戦」の印を書き込むようなものだ。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — The New York Giants could practically mark an ‘L’ on their schedule each season as soon as they saw their date in Philadelphia.


              It's been automatic.


              The Eagles have beaten the Giants 13 straight times at home — including one playoff win — since New York last won on Oct. 27, 2013.


              Maybe not this season. 


              The Giants (4-2-1) come to Philadelphia on Sunday as betting favorites and in first place in the woeful NFC East. If the Giants win, they'd practically have a stranglehold in a division where no other team has a winning record, and they have yet to lose to Washington or Dallas. 


              Are the Giants getting cocky and complacent in coach John Harbaugh's first season?


              “I do think that that’s definitely something to get locked in on,” Harbaugh said, “but I don’t believe it is this week.”


              Long the class of the NFC East, the Eagles (2-6) are on a six-game losing streak and set to start their third quarterback of the season — the fourth one who'll take snaps.


              Eagles coach Nick Sirianni had promised that everything was on the table when it came to trying to get his team rolling again. He instead kept beleaguered offensive coordinator Sean Mannion as the play-caller but benched Tanner McKee after he went 0-3 since taking over as the starter when Jalen Hurts was sidelined for the season because of blood clots.


              The move came roughly 48 hours after Sirianni said McKee was their guy and a change at the position was not coming.


              Joe Milton is now tasked with saving the Eagles' season.


              Just maybe the Eagles could see a path toward a division title if they knock off the Giants. NFL history suggests it's unlikely. Only three teams that started 2-6 have ever made the playoffs.


              The 26-year-old Milton has appeared in five NFL games in relief, including Dallas’ season finale at the Giants in January, when he was 7 of 13 for 73 yards and an interception.


              “He works extremely hard,” Sirianni said. “He’s always in the building doing the extra things, and I like his progression.”


              Milton was oh-so briefly a teammate with Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy in 2020 at Michigan. Milton transferred to Tennessee while McCarthy would lead the Wolverines to a national title. 


              Much like the Eagles, the Giants have churned through quarterbacks, going from Jaxson Dart (injured) to Jameis Winston (benched) before settling on McCarthy. He'll make his second start of the season, a veteran compared to Milton's first career start after mostly playing garbage time in two previous stops.


              Milton’s job is to give the Eagles at least a glimmer of hope of keeping their playoff hopes alive.

articles.headline: Stumbling Texans and winless Chargers meet in a matchup of NFL disappointments
articles.description: — The Houston Texans and Los Angeles...
articles.headlineJa: 不振のテキサンズと白星のないチャージャーズ、NFLの期待外れ同士が激突
articles.descriptionJa: — ヒューストン・テキサンズとロサンゼルス...
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — The Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers began the season with legitimate playoff and Super Bowl expectations. After stumbling through the first half, they're in salvage mode as two of the biggest disappointments in the NFL.


              The Texans made the playoffs three years in a row — a franchise best — and won the AFC South two of those years before opening this season 0-4. The Chargers won 11 games and reached the playoffs in each of coach Jim Harbaugh's first two seasons, but are the league's only remaining winless team.


              The underperformers meet Sunday at SoFi Stadium.


              The Texans (2-5) are happily on the road coming off their bye week, having gone 0-4 at home. The Chargers (0-7) have dropped 10 straight overall dating to last season. 


              “We’ve been in a lot of close games,” Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. “How do you find yourself on the winning side of those games? Being great in situational football and finishing the proper way. If we do those things, that’s when you earn the right to win games.”


              No team starting 0-7 or worse has ever made the NFL playoffs. At this point, the Bolts would settle for a touchdown. They've gone nine quarters and 27 drives without one. Their last came in the third quarter of a 23-17 loss to Denver on Oct. 11.


              “Want to win, want to get the ball in the end zone,” coach Jim Harbaugh said. “Focused on getting it turned, forging ahead and really striving in every way to play winning football.”


              The Chargers failed to show signs of life coming out of their Week 7 bye, losing to the Los Angeles Rams 24-9 last weekend. Justin Herbert passed for a season-best 257 yards, but also had two more interceptions, giving him a league-high 10 for the season. He has thrown at least one in every game so far.


              Conversely, Houston QB C.J. Stroud is among the league's top passers, with 11 TDs and just one interception. The Texans' self-inflicted wounds include a non-existent ground game and foolish penalties.


              "Focus on the little things, fix those, and I think we'll be fine,” said Stroud, who spent last weekend in Los Angeles watching his alma mater Ohio State get upset by USC.


              The Texans have lost wide receiver Jaylin Noel (turf toe) for the season after he got hurt in a 27-21 overtime loss to the New York Giants. He generated explosiveness on offense and production as a kick and punt returner.


              “We’re going to feel it,” Stroud said. “It sucks that he’s starting to really find himself and then to go down like that.”


              Harbaugh is 0-7 as a coach for the first time, but he endured an identical stretch of losing as quarterback for the Chargers in 2000 when they began 0-7 in San Diego. That team finished 1-15.

articles.headline: Panthers place focus on stopping the run vs. Broncos following defensive coordinator change
articles.description: — Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales offered one overriding requisition to Todd Wash after promoting him to interim defensive coordinator last week: "Stop the run."
articles.headlineJa: パンサーズ、ディフェンス・コーディネーター交代を受け、ブロンコスのラン阻止に注力
articles.descriptionJa: — キャロライナ・パンサーズのデイブ・カニレス監督は、先週トッド・ウォッシュを暫定ディフェンス・コーディネーターに昇格させた際、彼に唯一の至上命題として「ランを阻止しろ」と命じた。
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales offered one overriding requisition to Todd Wash after promoting him to interim defensive coordinator last week: "Stop the run."


              That's something the Panthers struggled to do under Ejiro Evero, and it ultimately cost him his job.


              The Panthers (3-4) enter Sunday's game against the surging Denver Broncos (6-2) ranked 30th in the league against the run, while allowing the fifth-most points in the league.


              It's now up to Wash to fix it.


              Canales made the change at coordinator just hours after the Panthers suffered their second straight loss last Thursday night to the Green Packers, 27-19. The timing of the move gave Wash a few extra days to make changes.


              Just how dramatically different the Panthers will look on Sunday remains to be seen, as players and coaches alike have been predictably coy when it comes to the game plan.


              “I guess we will have to see Sunday,” defensive lineman Derrick Brown said with a grin.


              There's speculation the Panthers could begin to transition away from Evero's 3-4 base scheme to the 4-3 scheme Wash used during his previous stint as an NFL defensive coordinator with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2016-2020).


              But Brown said that's easier said than done in the middle of an NFL season.


              “I don’t think that’s what we’re doing,” Brown said the idea of shifting to a base 4-3 defense, “So it’s one of those things where we just got a few different tweaks here and there, but for the most part we’re going to do what we did.”


              Wash seemed to echo that sentiment, while still leaving the door open to change.


              “We are who we are,” Wash said in reference to the team's defensive personnel which is made up heavily of outside linebackers. “(But) we will try to throw some wrinkles in.”


              The Broncos enter the game on a four-game win streak despite an offense that ranks 30th in the league overall and 26th in rushing.


              However, Bo Nix and company seem to be hitting their stride.


              Denver has scored 58 points over the past two weeks.


              Jonah Coleman took on a bigger role in the backfield in the Broncos' 28-24 come-from-behind win over Kansas City, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching four passes for 63 yards.


              Nix's latest comeback propelled the Broncos into sole possession of first place in the AFC West. The Panthers (3-4) are also alone in first in the NFC South despite a losing record.


              Nix described the Broncos as being a “mature team" and isn't expecting a letdown against Carolina.

articles.description: Manchester United are reportedly looking at a move for Manchester City defender Rayan Aït-Nouri. Transfer Talk has the latest.

articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは、マンチェスター・シティのディフェンダー、ラヤン・アイ・ヌリの獲得を検討していると報じられている。「トランスファー・トーク」が最新情報をお届けする。
articles.body:
Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals Manchester United, while Como center back Jacobo Ramón has caught the eye of Manchester United, Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri could join rivals Manchester United, as he is seeking an exit in January, according to The Sun. Ait-Nouri, 25, has played only four times this season and has yet to appear in the Premier League. United are looking for a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw, and have been linked with Newcastle United's Lewis Hall, AFC Bournemouth's Adrien Truffert and Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, but could turn to the Algeria international.

- Manchester United are one of several clubs keen on signing Como center back Jacobo Ramón, TEAMtalk reports. The 21-year-old, who transfer is valued at around €50 million, impressed the Red Devils during Como's 4-1 UEFA Champions League victory over them last month. Chelsea are also keen, while Arsenal, Liverpool and Fulham are monitoring his development in Italy. However, his former club Real Madrid are considering exercising their option to re-sign him next summer, potentially complicating any move from Premier League clubs.

- Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United have stepped up their scouting of Galatasaray attacking midfielder Alexsey Batrakov, according to TEAMtalk. All three clubs watched the 21-year-old score twice against Stuttgart on Tuesday evening in the UEFA Champions League. The Russia international is reported to have a release clause worth €60 million, although a January departure is considered unlikely as Gala are looking to open talks over an improved contract and could seek to remove the clause as part of any new agreement.

- Everton are interested in signing Palmeiras striker Vitor Roque in 2027, as per Diario Sport. The Brazilian club are unwilling to open negotiations at less than €50 million for the 21-year-old, whose contract runs until December 2029. A move could also provide a windfall for his former club Barcelona, who retained 20% of his economic rights after his move to Palmeiras last year and would receive €10 million from a transfer at that price. Roque has scored five goals in 19 league matches this season.

- Liverpool are in advanced talks with 19-year-old midfielder Trey Nyoni over a contract extension, according to The Athletic. Discussions have been ongoing for several months, with all parties optimistic that an agreement will be reached, although nothing has been finalized. Nyoni has more than 3½ years remaining on his current deal, but Liverpool want to reward his progress under Andoni Iraola. The club rejected a £30 million offer from Nottingham Forest to sign him in the summer.

articles.headline: Bronny James assigned to Coachella Valley Lakers in G League
articles.description: The Los Angeles Lakers have used Bronny James sparingly during their 7-2 start and on Thursday assigned him to their G League affiliate, the Coachella Valley Lakers.
articles.headlineJa: ブローニー・ジェームズ、Gリーグのコーチエラ・バレー・レイカーズにアサイン
articles.descriptionJa: ロサンゼルス・レイカーズは、7勝2敗と好調な滑り出しを見せる中でブローニー・ジェームズの起用を限定的にしており、木曜日にGリーグの提携チームであるコーチエラ・バレー・レイカーズへ彼をアサインした。
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have used Bronny James sparingly during their 7-2 start and on Thursday assigned him to their G League affiliate, the Coachella Valley Lakers.

The 22-year-old third-year guard has averaged just 2.4 minutes and 0.8 points per game in five appearances for the Lakers, who have joined the Portland Trail Blazers (6-1) and Houston Rockets (7-2) atop the Western Conference standings in the early going.

James has performed better in the developmental G League, averaging 18.4 points on 49.6% shooting (including 41.3% from 3), 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 25 games the past two seasons for the South Bay Lakers, who were rebranded and relocated this season. The team plays its home games at Acrisure Arena in Palm Desert, rather than at the Lakers' practice facility in El Segundo.

Coachella Valley opens its season Friday at home against the Salt Lake City Stars. Beyond a new home arena, the Lakers' G League affiliate also has a new coach. Alex Cerda was named as the successor to Zack Guthrie after Guthrie joined coach JJ Redick's staff with the Lakers.

Lakers rookie Cameron Carr also was assigned to Coachella Valley on Thursday.

articles.headline: Jonathan Taylor turns trade talk into 'regular scheduled programming' as Colts and Cowboys meet
articles.description: — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins.
articles.headlineJa: コルツとカウボーイズが交渉を進める中、ジョナサン・テイラーはトレードの噂を「日常茶飯事」として捉える
articles.descriptionJa: — トレードの噂が飛び交う中でも、ジョナサン・テイラーはフットボールをプレーすることに慣れてきた。
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins.


              This week, he has heard his named linked to multiple teams, heard about “done deals” and heard some question whether it's wise to even play Sunday when the struggling Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys meet — two days before this season's trade deadline.


              So Taylor has learned how to laugh it off. All he wants to do is give the fans something to cheer.


              “It's kind of dragged on for a while now, so at this point, it's just noise,” Taylor said Thursday about the chatter. “It's been like three or four or however many weeks, so at this point, it becomes regular scheduled programming.”


              It wasn't supposed to be this way after the seven-year veteran who has never played for another team signed a two-year contract extension worth $44 million to stay with the Colts in August.


              Even then, this week's featured matchup was supposed to be about the brother bash: Indy's veteran receiver Josh Downs and Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs. But with both teams reeling, the older brother requesting a trade and the younger brother in the concussion protocol and dealing with a bad ankle, their dream story may have to wait.


              That puts the spotlight on Taylor, the franchise's No. 2 career rusher in what could be his final game playing in the Colts — though it's not something he has contemplated.


              “We've got an opportunity, especially this week — especially after last week — to come back and put a better product on the field,” he said, referring to the embarrassing 42-7 loss to Jacksonville. “That's my biggest goal. Last week was tough. You know you never want to go and put that on display."


              He just wants to give fans something to cheer about. Indy has (2-6) lost four straight and 13 of 15 and the last time they were home, the boobirds were out in force.


              Dallas (3-5) hasn't played much better lately. It has the league's worst run defense and has lost three of four after blowing a lead and losing 33-30 in overtime at Arizona last week. So coach Brian Schottenheimer would like nothing better than to ruin Indy's homecoming — even if it Taylor's last stand.


              “There are certainly a lot of things we as a football team can do better," he said, noting the Cowboys' rushing disparity from Week 7 to Week 8. “I didn’t think we did a great job tackling. And then there’s certainly things that I can do better in all facets, No. 1 being find a way to finish the game and give us a chance.”


              Need to know
              Dalals (3-5) at Indianapolis (2-6)


              When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox.


              Latest odds: Cowboys by 5½.


              Against the spread: Cowboys 4-4; Colts 4-4.


              Last week: Cowboys lost to Cardinals 33-30 in OT; Colts lost to Jaguars 42-7

articles.headline: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice files for bankruptcy, claims he owes over $3.45M in debts
articles.description: Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts.
articles.headlineJa: チーフスのWRラシー・ライスが破産申請、345万ドル超の負債を主張
articles.descriptionJa: チーフスのワイドレシーバー、ラシー・ライスが連邦裁判所に破産を申請し、345万ドルを超える負債があると主張した。
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court Wednesday, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts, according to federal court records.

Rice, who filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, claimed more than $2.1 million of his debts are tied to varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations that have either been settled or are awaiting trial.

Rice, 26, has been sued by multiple individuals for his role in a high-speed multicar crash in Dallas in 2024 and an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025.

In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in "deferred compensation." The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property.

Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for "individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors," according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt.

The documents claim Rice's largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit.

According to the documents, Rice used his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral with Thomas McMurray, his attorney in the pending civil litigations.

Rice's bankruptcy attorney, David Shuster, and the Chiefs had no comment about the bankruptcy filing. McMurray did not immediately respond to messages left by ESPN seeking comment.

Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract with the Chiefs and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026. He has played in five games this season, with 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns.

articles.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. 

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Nov. 5

Wemby makes MVP opening statement

Victor Wembanyama officially launched his 2027 NBA MVP campaign on Wednesday with a statistical performance not seen since Wilt Chamberlain.

The Spurs star posted 52 points, 24 rebounds and eight blocks in a 112-111 victory over the Dallas Mavericks, becoming the first player to achieve a 52/24/8 line since blocks became an official statistic in 1973-74.

Chamberlain, the Hall of Fame center, is the only player in league history to match or exceed those numbers thanks to a 55-point, 29-rebound, 17-block performance for the Philadelphia Warriors against the New York Knicks in 1961.

This was truly rare air: Wembanyama posted the NBA's first 52/24 line since Chamberlain in 1969 and the first 50-20 game since Luka Doncic in 2022.

"It should be more like this," Wembanyama promised. "More often."

With Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander emerging as early MVP favorites, Wembanyama threw his hat into the ring on a wild night that easily could have gotten even wilder. The 2023 No. 1 pick set a new career high for scoring by shooting 16-of-28 from the field and 19-of-23 from the free throw line against an overmatched Dallas front line, but he made only one of his eight 3-point attempts.

"I can still do more," Wembanyama said, noting that he's shooting a career-low 24 percent on 3-pointers this season. "My shots weren't falling tonight and that forces me into a style of play that is exhausting. I can do it. The proof is there."

After stumbling out of the gate with an 0-2 start, the Spurs have won six straight games and Wembanyama has started to find his scoring groove. The Thunder held the French center to 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting on opening night, but he has scored at least 36 points in three of his past four games and is on track to lead the NBA in blocks for the fourth straight season.

Go ahead and brace for more fireworks: Wembanyama and the Spurs are set to face the NBA's three worst defenses -- the Kings, Suns and Bulls -- over the next week.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third in MVP voting last season and is seeking to become the award's youngest winner since Derrick Rose in 2011.

articles.headline: LeBron James' reps send cease-and-desist letter to 'Bron AI' sports betting app
articles.description: LeBron James is aiming to get a sports betting app to stop using his likeness without authorization, a spokesperson for the 76ers star told Front Office Sports.
articles.body:
LeBron James is aiming to get a sports betting app to stop using his likeness without authorization, a spokesperson for the Philadelphia 76ers star told Front Office Sports.

The spokesperson said James "is in no way affiliated with this unauthorized use of his likeness" for the app, which is named Bron AI.

An advertisement for Bron AI shows a person resembling James -- wearing a No. 23 jersey with the name "Bron" on it -- from behind as he uses the app, which is designed to offer sports betting picks and research by aggregating data from traditional sportsbooks and prediction markets.

Attorney Lawrence Shire issued a cease-and-desist letter on James' behalf to PlayVision Inc., a copy of which was obtained by Front Office Sports. In the letter, Shire writes that the company has "been making unauthorized use and illicit exploitation of our Client's name, nickname, likeness, image, persona, and other identifying attributes, materials and related information (collectively, the 'Client ID') to create an association between Company and our Client."

Shire writes that the ad implies that James "is involved with betting on basketball, which is a very serious violation of NBA rules and regulations." The letter asks the company to cease using all forms of James' likeness and name by 5:30 p.m. Thursday.

A social media post with the advertisement had been taken off the Bron AI Instagram account as of Thursday afternoon.

Adam Mendelsohn, James' longtime media adviser, acknowledged that the Bron AI app may have been intentionally trying to draw a cease and desist to "make it a story."

"You would prefer not to respond but you don't have a choice in a situation like this," Mendelsohn told Front Office Sports. "It's not the first time, and it won't be the last. For what it's worth, these gimmicks never work because people see through it."

Bron AI and PlayVision did not respond to requests for comment from Front Office Sports.

James recently signed a marketing deal with prediction market platform Polymarket. Prior to that, he had served as a brand ambassador for DraftKings starting in January 2024.

articles.description: What are we watching this week? Man United are hoping for a rally, Como are magical to watch, PSG are the team to beat and we're worried about Gianluigi Donnarumma.
articles.headlineJa: サッカー界の主役たち：マン・U、コモ、PSG、ドンナルマ
articles.descriptionJa: 今週の注目は何？マン・Uは巻き返しを狙い、コモの戦いぶりは魔法のように魅力的で、PSGは攻略すべき強敵、そして我々はジャンルイジ・ドンナルマのことが心配だ。
articles.body:
It's getting ridiculous in the best possible way. With each passing year, seemingly as teams realize that the extended Champions League league phase offers plenty of leeway if they lose a game or two, the guardrails slip a little bit more.

In 2024-25, teams averaged 1.63 goals per game in the league phase, a robust amount but not dramatically off of what we see in domestic leagues. In 2025-26, it was 1.69.

This year, through four matchdays, teams are averaging 2.02 goals per match and on Wednesday alone, six of nine matches saw at least five combined goals scored.

There were three 3-2 matches, including Fenerbahce's comeback win over Liverpool and lovely back-and-forth away wins for Manchester City (over RB Leipzig) and Real Madrid (over AEK Athens). And of course, there was Como's eye-popping 9-1 in over poor Lens; in their first Champions League campaign, the Italian side have scored 19 goals in their first four matches, winning three.

- UCL Talking Points: Are Como the real deal?

- Yamal makes more history for ruthless Barcelona

- Soccer's rich history of fan protests

The lack of consequence certainly has something to do with all this swashbuckling play, but maybe it's rubbed off on the rest of Europe? The season is still young, but scoring is up 7.8% in Ligue 1, 8.0% in the Bundesliga, 10.0% in LaLiga, and a whopping 20.1% in the Eredivisie and 23.9% in Serie A. Most of the increase has come from open-play, too -- it's not like teams are just earning a lot more penalties or something. (Meanwhile, Premier League scoring is actually down 2% so far this season. Fuddy duds.)

This is certainly a trend worth looking into, but for now I just want to say ... thank you. Goals are fun.

Let's once again look at five of soccer's main characters following another rousing Champions League matchday.

Main character No. 1: Manchester United's path forward

Ninety minutes is a long time. It's easy to forget that when you're an American fan accustomed to 3.5-hour American football games, but on Tuesday at Old Trafford, 90 minutes was long enough for Manchester United to play maybe their most listless 45 minutes of the 2020s (a high bar to clear), watch their fans rain tennis balls onto the pitch in protest of administrative incompetence and a nine-match winless streak, grab a lifeline in the form of a penalty, miss said penalty, take advantage of a second chance via VAR, spend a good 20 minutes blowing a number of great chances to tie, and still have enough time left to tie, take the lead and hold on for what might (or might not) be a season-saving and trajectory-defining win.

Roma's two early goals made United look completely hapless, and when United fell behind 2-0, it almost looked as if Bruno Fernandes started trying to pick a fight and land a red card so he wouldn't have to watch the rest of the match. It even took Fernandes a second penalty attempt to get the home team on the board.

articles.headline: Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international soccer with Portugal after being benched by coach Jorge Jesus. It is far from the first high-profile row of his career.
articles.body:
Editor's note: This has been updated after Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international soccer on Nov. 5, 2026.

Was it always going to end like this? Cristiano Ronaldo -- Portugal's greatest-ever player, who led them to victory at the 2016 UEFA European Championship, and won the UEFA Champions League and the Ballon d'Or five times in a glittering club career -- has called time on his international career.

Ronaldo, 41, walked away from the national team's camp last month after a row with coach Jorge Jesus. The Portugal boss insisted there was "no issue," but admitted mistakes in his handling of Ronaldo's role in the 2-1 win over Norway in the UEFA Nations League on Sept. 27, when he was an unused substitute.

Despite it seeming as though the coach and his captain had patched things up, Ronaldo confirmed Thursday that he has played his last game for Portugal. However, an acrimonious end to his international career -- during which he has scored a men's record 146 goals -- could hardly be described as a shock.

- Ronaldo's incredible Portugal career: Best moments, key stats

- Siuuuu! The story of Ronaldo's career at Portugal, Man Utd, Real Madrid

- Ronaldo goal tracker: Every step on the road to 1,000 career goals

Managing the transition when an aging superstar's performance level drops is never easy, and Ronaldo's role and impact -- positive and negative -- with Portugal had been debated for three successive major tournaments: in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

Throughout his 25-year career, Ronaldo has been involved in a series of headline-grabbing disagreements with managers, teammates and executives. With his latest drama seemingly resolved, here are some of the most high-profile previous examples.

Unhappy Ronaldo backs Blatter's insensitive "slavery" comparison (July 10, 2008)

Ronaldo's bid to leave Manchester United for Real Madrid that summer reached a new, histrionic high -- or low -- when Ronaldo echoed comments from then-FIFA president Sepp Blatter that keeping a player at a club against their will was comparable to "modern slavery." Ronaldo told Portugal's TV1: "It's true. I agree with what the president of FIFA said. I know what I want and what I would like. We have to see what happens. I do not know where I will begin next season." After five successful years at Old Trafford, Ronaldo was ready to move on, but United stood firm and the forward had to wait another season before his desired move to the Bernabéu was finally fulfilled.

Ronaldo subs himself off mid-game at Old Trafford (Dec. 6, 2008)

Ronaldo abruptly walked off the pitch -- and headed straight down the tunnel -- midway through Manchester United's 1-0 win over Sunderland at Old Trafford. The team were left playing with 10 men, as United's coaching staff rushed to organise an unexpected substitution. articles.headline: Thursday's fantasy hoops adds, NBA bets to make: Black, da Silva worth streaming
articles.description: Eric Moody breaks down Thursday's NBA slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and his favorite bets.
articles.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Thursday

Klay Thompson makes his return to Golden State, where he won four championships. His Miami Heat are coming off an overtime win against the LA Clippers. In the only other game of the night, the Phoenix Suns will try to snap a four-game losing streak when they host the Orlando Magic. Both the Heat and Suns are playing on the second night of a back-to-back.

The Magic have lost two straight and remain without Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs. Franz Wagner has stepped up, averaging 20.3 PPG and 7.6 APG, and Anthony Black is off the injury report after missing Monday's game against the Washington Wizards. The Suns lost 132-119 to the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday despite 33 points from Devin Booker. Phoenix ranks last in defensive rating.

The Heat have won three of their last four games after starting the season 0-4. Thompson scored 30 points and made eight 3-pointers in Wednesday's win over the Clippers, including the game-winner in overtime. Bam Adebayo added 35 points and 10 rebounds, while Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 27 points and 14 rebounds. Miami now faces a Golden State Warriors team that has won five straight. The short turnaround could be a challenge for Miami after Wednesday's overtime game.

Let's take a closer look at both matchups, along with some fantasy streamers and betting angles worth considering.

Fantasy stream team

Players available in at least 50% of leagues

 Anthony Black, PG/SG, Orlando Magic (rostered in 50.8% of ESPN leagues)

We're just over the roster threshold here. Black has taken on a larger with Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs sidelined. He has contributed as a scorer, playmaker and defender, finishing with at least 37 fantasy points in three of his last four games. Black sat out Monday's matchup against Washington, but he's off the injury report for Thursday's game against Phoenix.

 Dillon Brooks, SF/SG, Phoenix Suns (38.1%)

Brooks has scored at least 29 fantasy points in three of his last four games and played 33 or more minutes in three of them. He's still seeing solid usage despite sharing the floor with Devin Booker and Jalen Green. Brooks is worth streaming for points and 3-pointers, though he's better suited for points leagues than category leagues.

 Pelle Larsson, SG/SF, Miami Heat (15.6%)

Larsson has been useful in points leagues, but I prefer him in category formats. He won't score as much as Black or Tristan da Silva, but he chips in rebounds, assists and steals without hurting you in turnovers. Larsson is averaging 30.4 MPG despite coming off the bench, and that playing time should continue Thursday against a Warriors team is 22nd in defensive rating.

articles.headline: Mikel Arteta: Viktor Gyökeres 'really needed' a good Arsenal performance
articles.description: Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres "needed" a good performance after he starred in the 2-1 Champions League win at Slavia Prague.
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta has admitted Arsenal forward Viktor Gyökeres "needed" a good performance after he starred in the 2-1 Champions League win at Slavia Prague.

Sweden striker Gyökeres made one goal and scored the other in one of his best displays since joining Arsenal in July 2025.

The 28-year-old has played second fiddle to Kai Havertz this season and had scored only one goal before Wednesday night, in the Carabao Cup penalty shoot-out defeat at Fleetwood last month.

But against Slavia, Gyökeres laid on the opener for Noni Madueke before scoring a stylish second on a hugely encouraging evening in the Czech capital.

"I thought he was really good," Arteta told reporters. "It was a game we believed would be really good for him, for the demands the opponent puts in and the spaces he could use.

"He's done it really well, not just for the assist and the goal, but he was really connected to the team. It's really great news for him, because he really needed that performance.

"He did that really well, understood really well when to appear, when to threaten, because they leave people, they follow man-to-man in the midfield and leave spaces there.

"So when I said he was really connected to the team, that was another example. I thought he had a great performance alongside the goal and assist.

"I'd imagine every player wants to play every game, and Viktor is no different. The players need to impact the game like he has done when they get the opportunity, to show the level they can produce. It's really positive for the team."

- Arteta: 'A lot to learn' from Arsenal's 'sloppy' win over Slavia Prague

- Kuyt hails 'another miracle in Istanbul' after Fenerbahce beat former club Liverpool

- Haaland tells Man City to 'step up' after netting winner in Leipzig

Despite his lack of minutes on the pitch, Gyökeres has now contributed to five goals in his last five matches.

"I feel very good," he told Arsenal's website. "Obviously, I'm happy with the win and to contribute to the two goals."

Premier League leaders Arsenal are up to third in the Champions League table despite a wobble in the second half, when Wiktor Nowak's 90th-minute goal left them clinging on throughout stoppage time.

"A good feeling in the first half -- and then obviously in the second half, with how that went, maybe the feeling isn't as good. But overall, if you look at the first half, it's a good feeling," added Gyökeres.

"It's my job as a striker and of course I want to contribute every game when I'm on the pitch and want to be involved as much as I can in attacks.

"So far we've had a good run in the Champions League and in the league as well.

"At the stage we're in right now, we're in a good spot, but I think we're all clear on what we can improve and what we need to do to take the next step."

articles.headline: Jack Grealish won't return for Everton this weekend - David Moyes
articles.description: Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday.
articles.body:
Jack Grealish remains unavailable for Everton's Premier League clash with Coventry on Friday.

The on-loan Manchester City midfielder has missed the Toffees' last two games -- both against Newcastle, in the Carabao Cup and the league -- following a breach of club discipline.

The club have given few details about the situation other than to say the 31-year-old was "not match-fit" prior to Monday's victory at St James' Park.

Manager David Moyes was again reluctant to discuss the matter at a press conference on Thursday but did confirm the England international would not feature against the Sky Blues at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Moyes said: "No, Jack is not available. I wouldn't give you the plan but we will be working with Jack again soon."

Asked if the upcoming international break could give Everton the opportunity to resolve the issue, Moyes added: "We just need to wait and see how things go."

- There is a way back for Jack Grealish after another Everton omission - David Moyes ESPN News Services

- Jack Grealish misses Everton-Newcastle due to 'breach of club discipline'

Moyes is hopeful defender Jarrad Branthwaite will be available after he was withdrawn with cramp in the latter stages on Monday.

He said: "We're just nursing him along a wee bit, just checking to see he's OK. We need to see how he is."

articles.headline: Harry Kane signs new Bayern Munich contract: 'I want to win many more titles'
articles.description: Harry Kane has signed a new contract to commit his future to Bayern Munich until 2029.
articles.body:
Harry Kane has signed a new contract to commit his future to Bayern Munich until 2029.

ESPN had previously reported that the Ballon d'Or winner, 33, was close to extending his stay with the German giants, after he entered the final season of the four-year deal he signed when joining Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023.

The England captain won football's top individual prize -- becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to do so -- after scoring 73 goals last season.

He ended his personal trophy drought by winning the Bundesliga in 2025 and 2026, and also won the German Cup last season. Kane scored 100 goals in Germany's top flight in the fewest games ever, managing the feat in just 98 appearances.

Kane also recently matched the record, held by Peter Shilton since 1990, for the most England caps after a 125th appearance against Czechia in the most recent international break. He was already his country's top goalscorer with a tally that stands at 91 goals.

Kane has scored 12 times for Bayern so far this season, giving him a tally of 156 goals in 161 appearances for the club.

"I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane said. "I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

Herbert Hainer, FC Bayern president, said: "What began as a major transfer has, over time, become a special chapter in FC Bayern's history. Harry Kane lives up to every promise football has to offer, and he has secured his place in the hearts of the fans as one of the greatest figures in the sport of our time. My compliments to Jan-Christian Dreesen and our sporting management team. This is a special moment for FC Bayern today."

Jan-Christian Dreesen, FC Bayern CEO, said: "We're delighted to have successfully extended Harry Kane's contract. This is fantastic news for us, for our fans and for the Bundesliga. The Ballon d'Or winner is staying at Bayern Munich! Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and as a role model both on and off the pitch. He has long since made FC Bayern his home, has continued to develop with us and crowned that development with the Ballon d'Or. His contract extension is a commitment to FC Bayern and to a story that is far from over."

Max Eberl, FC Bayern board member for sport, said: "This key contract extension gives us certainty in our planning. It sends a message that the biggest goals are within reach at FC Bayern. Players like Harry Kane offer a team unique opportunities. We're delighted that he will continue to be a key figure who helps shape the direction of the club, and with whom we can continue to build our squad for the future."

articles.headline: Fantasy basketball rookie watch: Who's standing out and who's worth monitoring
articles.description: Eric Moody highlights which rookies are standing out in the early part of the NBA season, and which are worth rostering now or down the road.
articles.body:
The first two weeks of the season have already shown how differently these rookies are being used. Some have stepped into significant roles and are delivering for fantasy managers. Others are struggling with their shot or simply aren't getting enough minutes to make an impact.

Let's rank the top 15 rookies based primarily on their rest-of-season value in points leagues, with some consideration for category formats.

We'll also look at which players could become more fantasy relevant as the season progresses.

1. Caleb Wilson, SF, Chicago Bulls

Chicago hasn't wasted any time putting Wilson to work. The rookie has 19.5 PPG and 6.5 RPG in 34.1 MPG. He's also attempted 17.1 shots with a 26.3% usage rate. The shooting hasn't been particularly efficient, and averaging more than three combined steals and blocks will be difficult to sustain. Still, Wilson is getting plenty of opportunities on both ends of the floor. He's an automatic starter in fantasy lineups and has a chance to be especially valuable in category leagues.

2. Cameron Boozer, PF, Memphis Grizzlies

The shooting hasn't caught up with the rest of Boozer's game, but fantasy managers have a lot to like. He's averaged 16.5 PPG, 9.8 RPG and 5.4 assists while making 2.3 3-pointers per game. His 23.4% assist percentage shows how much Memphis relies on him as a passer. Boozer is also shooting 94.4% from the free throw line, which helps offset his field goal percentage below 40%. He's a strong hold in every format and someone I'd consider trading for if another manager is frustrated with his shooting.

3. Darius Acuff Jr., PG, Sacramento Kings

Sacramento has essentially given Acuff the keys to its offense. He's averaged 25.6 PPG, 7.0 APG and 3.0 3-pointers in 36.6 MPG, with a 32.3% usage rate. Acuff recently scored 38 points with nine 3-pointers against the Grizzlies. The downside is his efficiency. Acuff's shooting 37.7% from the field and committing 3.6 turnovers per game. That makes him more appealing in points leagues than category formats, but it's hard to argue with this kind of volume. Keep him in your starting lineup.

4. Yaxel Lendeborg, SF/PF, Golden State Warriors

Lendeborg has delivered in an expanded role for Golden State. He's averaged 21.5 PPG, 7.0 RPG, 3.9 APG and 2.5 3-pointers. Lendeborg's 63.8% true shooting percentage is impressive considering his offensive responsibilities. Jimmy Butler III's absence has helped create minutes and touches, and Lendeborg has played well. He's a must-start player, especially in category leagues. The one thing to watch is how much his role changes when Butler returns and Golden State's rotation gets healthier.

Dybantsa missed the start of the season with an ankle injury, but the No. 1 overall pick has looked comfortable offensively through three games. He's averaged 16.5 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 1.0 SPG in 30.5 minutes per game. His limited assists and 3-point production make him somewhat dependent on scoring r
